mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost varies by condition. Used 1NZ-FXE units typically cost £400-£900, reconditioned engines £1,200-£2,200, and fully rebuilt units £2,000-£3,500 supply-only. For the newer M15A-FXE engine, prices are slightly higher: used from £500, reconditioned from £1,400, rebuilt from £2,200. Fitting adds 6-8 hours of labour at UK specialist rates (£390-£520). Always confirm the hybrid system calibration is included.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of head gasket failure in a Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs are engine overheating, white smoke from the exhaust (coolant burning), loss of coolant without external leaks, and milky oil from coolant contamination. Some early 2012-2014 1NZ-FXE engines are more prone to this issue. If you notice any of these symptoms, have the cooling system and head gasket checked immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2012-2017 Yaris 1.5 Hybrid worth £2,000-£8,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,000-£3,500 typically represents 25-50% of the vehicle's value - making replacement borderline on older examples but viable for newer or well-maintained cars. If the vehicle is worth under £5,000 and has other issues, evaluate scrap value first.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straight engine swap typically takes 6-8 working hours for a specialist workshop. Allow 2-3 days for the full process including diagnostics, removal, fitting, hybrid system calibration and road testing. Supply-only options are available for DIY or your own mechanic.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 1NZ-FXE and M15A-FXE Yaris Hybrid engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1NZ-FXE is a 1.5-litre four-cylinder engine used in the Mk3 (XP130) Yaris from 2012-2020, producing 100bhp. The M15A-FXE is a newer 1.5-litre three-cylinder Dynamic Force engine used in the Mk4 (XP210) Yaris from 2020 onwards, producing 116-130bhp. Both are full hybrids with eCVT transmission, but the M15A-FXE is built on Toyota's TNGA platform and offers improved efficiency and refinement.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a rebuilt Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine unit against manufacturing defects and component failure. Always confirm exact warranty terms - including labour coverage - with your chosen supplier before committing.

mainEntity.name: Why does my Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid keep getting a flat battery?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Yaris Hybrid's 12V auxiliary battery only charges when the car is in READY mode. Repeated short trips or leaving the car parked for extended periods can lead to a flat battery. This is the most common complaint on Yaris Hybrids and is easily fixed with a new 12V battery (£120-£200) - don't assume the main hybrid battery has failed.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid arrived in the UK in March 2012 as part of the third-generation (XP130) Yaris range - Toyota's first supermini to offer full hybrid power. With the fourth-generation (XP210) Yaris launched in 2020, the hybrid powertrain was completely redesigned around Toyota's TNGA platform, delivering improved efficiency and driving dynamics.

milestones.description: 1NZ-FXE 1.5-litre Atkinson-cycle hybrid launched with the Mk3 (XP130) Yaris. System output: 100bhp (74kW). Available in T4, Icon and Excel trims.
Mid-life update with revised 1NZ-FXE powertrain, improved efficiency and reduced CO2 emissions (89g/km).
Further refinement of the 1.5 Hybrid system with updated CVT calibration and improved refinement.
Fourth-generation (XP210) Yaris launched with all-new M15A-FXE 1.5-litre three-cylinder Dynamic Force hybrid engine. System output: 116bhp (85kW). Built on TNGA GA-B platform.
Uprated 130bhp (96kW) 1.5 Hybrid option introduced, marketed as 'Hybrid 130'.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - whether you drive an Icon, Design, Excel or GR Sport.

commonProblems.h2: Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid is one of the UK's most reliable superminis, but like any vehicle, it has a handful of known weak points. The 1NZ-FXE and M15A-FXE Atkinson-cycle hybrid engines are generally robust, but early head gasket issues on 1NZ-FXE units and 12V battery discharge are the most common owner-reported problems. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Head Gasket Failure - Why the Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid 1NZ-FXE Develops Gasket Issues
problems.rootCause: Some early 1NZ-FXE engines suffered premature head gasket failure, typically from coolant loss or overheating. The timing-chain-driven NZ engine can warp the head if the water pump weeps or the system runs low on coolant.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Cylinder head removal, gasket replacement, head inspection and resurfacing if warped. Labour-intensive due to hybrid system access.
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early and no internal damage. Typically restores full function for 40,000-60,000 miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine unit with upgraded components, addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When the engine has suffered significant internal damage from overheating or the vehicle has very high mileage.

problems.recommendation: For most Yaris 1.5 Hybrid owners with a 1NZ-FXE engine, a head gasket replacement at a specialist is the most cost-effective solution if caught early. Have the cooling system inspected at the first sign of coolant loss. If the engine has suffered internal damage from overheating, a rebuilt 1NZ-FXE unit with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty is the sensible long-term choice.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 1NZ-FXE Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid engine prices

problems.h4: 12V Auxiliary Battery Discharge - The Most Common Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid Niggle
problems.affectedModels: Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid (1NZ-FXE and M15A-FXE, all years)
problems.rootCause: The Yaris Hybrid's small 12V auxiliary battery only charges when the car is in READY mode - not when the engine is running. Repeated short trips or leaving the car parked for extended periods can lead to a flat battery.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Auxiliary battery replacement; resetting of systems.
repairOptions.longevity: Simple fix. New battery typically lasts 3-5 years.

repairOptions.dealerPrice: N/A - not applicable to this issue

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Not applicable - this is a low-cost repair that is worth doing on any vehicle.
problems.recommendation: If your Toyota Yaris 1.5 Hybrid won't start or shows warning lights, have the 12V auxiliary battery tested first - it's a £120-£200 fix and the most common cause of starting issues on these hybrids. Don't assume the main hybrid battery has failed.
